items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear and Chinese section headers help, but abbreviations are common (`st = apiGetStats()`, `est`, `inp`, `rem`). Markup builds long template strings with inline styles, and the refund preview formula has no comment.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: A single 2,671-line file, so capped at accept. Parts are reused, such as openConfirmModal and the api* functions. However, updateAfterSalePreview repeats the refund-allocation logic, there are many window.* globals and inline onclick handlers, and export/import handlers are duplicated for textarea and file.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Import is validated and returns errors, and actions return ok/error. However, FileReader has no onerror handler, money relies on float plus round2, and constants (95% member rate, coupon tiers) appear hardcoded. Nothing visible silently swallows errors.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: The breakdown shows the formula, rule hints and status badges, and reset uses openConfirmModal. But handleImportFromTextarea and handleFileUpload call apiImportData directly with no confirmation before overwriting data. After-sale submit also has no separate confirm step.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls the shared api* functions and stats come from apiGetStats each time. However, money uses floats plus round2 (`round2((reqOrigSum * order.payable) / order.subtotal)`), not integer cents, and the after-sale preview re-implements the refund calculation in the UI.
